records.abstractText:
Background

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by inflammatory signaling and metabolic adaptation within the tumor microenvironment. We integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to characterize inflammation-associated metabolic programs in PDAC.

Methods

Three public PDAC datasets were analyzed: TCGA-PAAD bulk RNA-seq data, GSE62452 tumor and adjacent tissue microarray data, and GSE154778 single-cell RNA-seq data from primary and metastatic PDAC. Kynurenine-, arachidonic acid-, inflammasome-, and glutamine-related transcriptional modules were evaluated. Cell-based qRT-PCR was used to validate selected inflammatory-metabolic genes after 48 h of cytokine stimulation.

Results

In GSE62452, 5985 of 33,297 probes were differentially expressed between tumor and adjacent tissues, including 3701 increased and 2284 decreased probes. Among selected targets, KYNU showed the largest increase. In 60 matched pairs, IDO1, KYNU, PTGS2, and PLA2G4A were significantly elevated in tumor tissues. Analysis of 14,926 single cells showed that myeloid cells had the highest mean scores across all four inflammatory-metabolic modules. Bulk expression patterns were positively associated across datasets (Spearman ρ=0.745, P = 0.0133). qRT-PCR further demonstrated cytokine-induced expression of selected inflammatory-metabolic genes.

Conclusions

Integrated bulk and single-cell analyses identify inflammation-associated metabolic transcriptional programs in PDAC, with prominent activity in myeloid cells. These findings provide a transcriptomic framework for future mechanistic and multi-omic validation rather than direct evidence of metabolic flux or clinical utility.

records.abstractText:
Objective

Focal autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP) mimics pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) radiologically, posing diagnostic challenges. This exploratory study investigated ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) for quantitative microvascular characterization and compared its diagnostic performance with that of conventional contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS).

Methods

In this prospective exploratory study, 30 patients with solid pancreatic lesions, including 15 with AIP and 15 with PDAC, underwent conventional ultrasound and CEUS followed by offline ULM reconstruction from arterial-phase raw RF data. Qualitative CEUS features and quantitative time-intensity curve parameters were assessed. Quantitative ULM parameters were extracted from lesion and matched perilesional pancreatic ROIs, and derived heterogeneity metrics were calculated. Histological vascular area fraction was quantified for correlation analysis. The diagnostic performances of CEUS and ULM parameters were evaluated and compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals.

Results

ULM showed significantly greater vascular density and more homogeneous intralesional vascular distribution in AIP than in PDAC (both p < 0.001). AIP also exhibited higher vessel ratio, perfusion index, fractal number, mean velocity, and mean diameter. Among the ULM parameters, the Δ fractal number and normalized fractal number showed the highest diagnostic performance, both achieving an AUC of 0.985. By comparison, the best-performing individual CEUS feature, enhancement intensity, yielded an AUC of 0.800, while its combination with washout pattern increased the AUC to 0.867. Among the quantitative CEUS parameters, half-intensity time and mean transit time performed best with AUCs of 0.880 and 0.864, respectively. ULM vessel ratio showed a significant positive correlation with histological vascular area fraction.

Conclusion

As a preliminary exploration, ULM demonstrated feasibility for characterizing microvascular differences and yielded higher diagnostic accuracy than CEUS parameters in a selected cohort. These findings require validation in larger, multicenter studies before ULM can be considered as a clinical biomarker for this differential diagnosis.

records.abstractText: BackgroundUpfront resection with adjuvant chemotherapy remains standard for resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), but a quarter or more of patients never start adjuvant therapy. We assessed readiness for adjuvant therapy within 12 weeks of upfront pancreatectomy, its correlates, and how often ready patients went untreated.MethodsWe reviewed 114 consecutive upfront pancreatectomies for PDAC at a high-volume centre (2017-2023). The primary endpoint was clinician-documented readiness for adjuvant chemotherapy within 12 weeks; initiation was secondary. The same oncologist usually documented both, so they are not independent. A burden score counted five adverse recovery events by day 30.ResultsOf 107 assessed patients, 89 (83.2%, 95% CI 74.7-89.7) were ready within 12 weeks (87.3% excluding 5 who died or had metastatic disease). Readiness was 94.6% with no adverse event, 82.4% with one, and 68.8% with two or more (non-readiness vs none: OR 7.1, 95% CI 2.1-30.5). Clinically relevant pancreatic fistula alone showed no association (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.36-3.33; 5 events), but a clinically important effect could not be excluded. The burden score had an internally estimated AUC of 0.73 (95% CI 0.59-0.85). Only 54 (50.5%) started chemotherapy within 12 weeks, including 53 of 88 ready patients.DiscussionMost patients were ready for adjuvant therapy within 12 weeks, and failure to recover tracked cumulative postoperative burden by day 30. Over a third of ready patients had no documented chemotherapy start, although readiness and initiation were not independently assessed. These hypothesis-generating findings require external validation and do not compare treatment sequencing.

records.abstractText:
Background and objectives

The association between time to treatment initiation (TTI) and metastatic progression in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the association between TTI and subsequent metastasis among patients undergoing curative-intent resection for PDAC.

Methods

Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries aged ≥ 66 years with nonmetastatic PDAC who underwent curative-intent resection from 2017 to 2021 were identified. TTI was defined as the interval from diagnosis to first cancer-directed treatment and modeled continuously per 30-day increase. Three-year metastatic progression was evaluated using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression, with death before metastasis as a competing event.

Results

Each 30-day increase in TTI was independently associated with a 14.2% higher subhazard of metastasis (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.142; 95% CI, 1.119-1.166; p < 0.001). The association persisted across surgery alone (sHR, 1.130), neoadjuvant therapy followed by surgery (sHR, 1.187), surgery followed by adjuvant therapy (sHR, 1.144), and trimodality therapy (sHR, 1.125) (all p < 0.001). In sensitivity analysis restricted to TTI ≤ 90 days, the association was attenuated and not statistically significant (sHR, 1.064; 95% CI, 0.964-1.174; p = 0.22).

Conclusions

Longer TTI was associated with increased metastatic progression across treatment pathways, although this association was attenuated among patients with TTI ≤ 90 days. Further studies are needed to determine whether treatment timing independently influences metastatic progression.

records.abstractText:
Background/aim

Although Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a promising therapeutic target in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), its longitudinal expression dynamics after chemotherapy remain unclear. In this study, we aimed to evaluate CLDN18.2 expression changes in paired pre- and post-chemotherapy specimens and to examine its clinicopathological and prognostic significance.

Patients and methods

We retrospectively analyzed 74 patients with PDAC who underwent pancreatectomy after preoperative chemotherapy at Kumamoto University Hospital between 2017 and 2024. CLDN18.2 protein expression was evaluated using immunohistochemistry assays in fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) samples obtained prior to chemotherapy and in corresponding resected specimens. The associations between CLDN18.2 expression levels and clinicopathological features were analyzed, along with longitudinal changes in CLDN18.2 expression.

Results

CLDN18.2 positivity was observed in 31 (41.9%) pre-treatment specimens and 18 (24.3%) post-treatment specimens. CLDN18.2 expression was not associated with any clinicopathological factor in the pre-treatment specimens. However, in the post-treatment specimens, CLDN18.2 positivity was significantly associated with well-differentiated tumors and lower pre-chemotherapy CA19-9 levels compared with CLDN18.2-negative cases. Neither overall survival nor recurrence-free survival differed significantly between the CLDN18.2-positive and CLDN18.2-negative groups. Paired analysis demonstrated that CLDN18.2 expression levels were significantly decreased in post-treatment specimens compared with pre-treatment specimens.

Conclusion

In our PDAC patient cohort, CLDN18.2 expression levels were significantly reduced following preoperative chemotherapy. These findings suggest that chemotherapy may alter CLDN18.2 expression patterns and may have implications for reassessing the CLDN18.2 status after treatment when considering future CLDN18.2 targeted therapy.

records.abstractText:
Introduction

Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is an established risk factor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). However, individual risk varies substantially, and the association between CP and PDAC is more complex than a uniform inflammation-driven pathway. Reverse causation, shared etiological factors, and biological heterogeneity may contribute to the observed association.

Areas covered

We critically review epidemiological, mechanistic, and causal evidence linking CP with PDAC, focusing on heterogeneity across CP subtypes and disease trajectories. We examine five domains potentially relevant to individual PDAC risk: genetic susceptibility, cumulative pancreatic injury, metabolic trajectories including new-onset diabetes, longitudinal imaging phenotypes, and emerging molecular alterations. We propose a multidomain framework for individualized and dynamic risk stratification and risk-adapted surveillance.

Expert opinion

CP should not be regarded as a uniformly high-risk condition for PDAC. Individual risk is shaped by the interaction of genetic, inflammatory, metabolic, structural, and molecular factors. The key question should therefore shift from whether CP increases PDAC risk to which patients are most likely to develop clinically consequential PDAC. Although multidomain and longitudinal assessment may enable targeted surveillance, most biomarkers and prediction strategies remain insufficiently validated. Prospective studies are required to determine whether this approach improves early detection and patient outcomes.

records.abstractText:
Objectives

Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog mutations drive over 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Direct RAS inhibitors have shown early activity, but the only prior meta-analysis pooled early-phase monotherapy cohorts and predates the first phase 3 randomized trial and newer combination regimens. We estimated the objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), and safety of Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog-targeted therapy in locally advanced or metastatic PDAC.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and SCOPUS were searched from inception through July 2026. Single-arm proportions were pooled using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model; RASolute 302 was analyzed separately. Prespecified subgroups stratified ORR by mechanistic class and line of therapy.

Results

A total of 1008 patients from 16 cohorts across 7 trials were included; 15 single-arm cohorts (507 patients) contributed to pooled estimates. Pooled ORR was 38.9% (95% CI: 29.9%-48.8%; I2=75.7%) and varied significantly by mechanism (P<0.0001): combination regimens showed the highest activity (60.5%), followed by G12D-selective (31.0%), pan-RAS(ON) (26.6%), and G12C-selective monotherapy (25.4%). Response declined with successive lines of therapy (P=0.0102), from 72.5% in treatment-naive patients to 32.5% after ≥3 prior lines. Pooled DCR was 87.6% (95% CI: 82.8%-91.2%). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 47.3%. In RASolute 302, daraxonrasib nearly doubled median overall survival versus chemotherapy (13.2 vs. 6.6 mo).

Conclusions

Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog-directed therapy produces meaningful antitumor activity in previously treated PDAC, greatest for combination regimens and earlier treatment; the evidence remains heterogeneous and largely early-phase, and randomized trials are needed before routine adoption.

records.abstractText:
Background

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is highly resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy due to its highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME).

Methods

Key regulatory genes were screened using bioinformatics analysis of TCGA and KEGG datasets. The expression patterns of HK2 were analyzed by single-cell sequencing and immunohistochemistry. The HK2-CCL5-CD8+ T-cell axis was evaluated using mouse pancreatic cancer models, in vitro co-culture systems, Transwell assays, RNA sequencing, and flow cytometry. The relationship between HK2 and anti-PD-1 therapy was also assessed.

Results

Hexokinase 2 (HK2), a rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis, is a key regulator in tumor immune evasion. HK2 is highly expressed in PDAC tumor cells. Its expression is significantly associated with CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the tumor microenvironment and disease progression. Inhibiting HK2 expression significantly promotes CC motif chemokine ligand 5 (CCL5) secretion by pancreatic cancer cells, which enhances the recruitment of CD8+ T-cell. Moreover, inhibiting HK2 enhance antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy in PDAC. Mechanistically, ROS scavenging with NAC reverses the CCL5 upregulation caused by HK2 inhibition, which in turn affects CD8+ T-cell infiltration.

Conclusion

Our study reveals a novel HK2-CCL5 axis that regulates CD8+ T-cell recruitment and shapes the immune microenvironment in PDAC.

records.abstractText: KRAS inhibitors represent a promising therapeutic frontier in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment. However, the clinical benefit of KRAS inhibitors in PDAC is limited by the frequent emergence of resistance. Here, we demonstrated that acquisition of resistance to KRAS inhibitors rendered PDAC cells hypersensitive to ferroptosis. Untargeted lipidomic profiling revealed that resistant cells underwent extensive lipid metabolic reprogramming characterized by selective enrichment of polyunsaturated fatty acid-containing phosphatidylcholines (PC-PUFAs) and a concomitant reduction in monounsaturated fatty acid-containing species (PC-MUFAs). The orphan nuclear receptor NR2F2 was a critical determinant of ferroptosis sensitivity in resistant cells. NR2F2 expression was markedly elevated upon acquisition of resistance, accompanied by substantial changes in its occupancy at regulatory elements of key lipid metabolic genes. By altering chromatin accessibility, NR2F2 drove PUFA biosynthesis and phospholipid remodeling, creating a ferroptosis-prone lipid state. Collectively, these findings establish NR2F2-driven lipid metabolic rewiring as an intrinsic ferroptosis liability in KRAS inhibitor-resistant PDAC and reveal ferroptosis induction as a therapeutic strategy to overcome resistance to KRAS-targeted therapies.

records.abstractText: Low-abundance exosomal proteins from trace plasma volumes remain challenging to profile by mass spectrometry. Here, we report a lanthanide metal-organic framework (Ln-MOF) functionalized with boronic acid and carboxylate dual ligands, which captures exosomal proteins via synergistic phosphate coordination, boronate-diol complexation, and cation-π interactions. Compared with traditional ultracentrifugation, which identifies 1003 proteins from 200 µL of plasma, the Ln-MOF method identifies 1523 proteins from only 50 µL of plasma. Notably, the method enriches glycoproteins and phosphoproteins by 2.1-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively. Applying this platform to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients and healthy controls, we delineate tumor tissue hypermetabolism vs. systemic immune suppression.

records.title: Single-cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal Cholesterol Metabolism Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma and Identify NSDHL as a Key Regulatory Gene
records.authorString: Gao Y, Li Z, Mu Y, Ren B, Li W, Zhou W.
records.abstractText: Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is one of the most lethal malignancies, and reprogramming of cholesterol metabolism plays a critical role in its malignant progression. However, the heterogeneity of cholesterol metabolism at the single-cell level and its key regulatory genes remain unclear. Methods This study integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk transcriptomic data (TCGA, GEO, ICGC) to systematically dissect the cellular landscape of cholesterol metabolism in PDAC. Malignant ductal epithelial cells were scored using five independent algorithms and divided into low (LCM), intermediate (ICM), and high (HCM) cholesterol metabolic subgroups. Cell communication, pseudotime trajectory, hdWGCNA, and XGBoost feature importance ranking were performed. Functional experiments including CCK-8, colony formation, EdU, wound healing, Transwell, and nude mouse tumor models were used to validate the role of NSDHL. Results Malignant ductal epithelial cells exhibited the highest cholesterol metabolic activity. The HCM subgroup showed enhanced communication with CAFs and endothelial cells, increased stemness, and coordinated activation of pro-tumor pathways (hypoxia, TNFα, NF-κB) and metabolic pathways (glycolysis, fatty acid synthesis). Pseudotime analysis revealed that cholesterol metabolism gradually increased along the LCM→ICM→HCM trajectory. Through hdWGCNA combined with XGBoost, NSDHL was identified as the most critical gene for the HCM phenotype. NSDHL was significantly overexpressed in PDAC tissues, enriched in high-malignancy regions, and correlated with poor prognosis. Knockdown of NSDHL significantly inhibited PDAC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and delayed tumor growth in nude mice. Conclusion This study reveals the heterogeneity landscape of cholesterol metabolism in PDAC and identifies NSDHL as a key gene driving the HCM phenotype and malignant progression, providing a new theoretical basis for prognosis evaluation and targeted therapy of PDAC.

records.abstractText: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is projected to become the second-leading cause of US cancer death by 2030, and survival is dominated by stage at diagnosis: roughly 44% at five years for localized disease versus about 3% with distant metastases. Only about 15% of cases are detected while localized, surgery reaches a minority of patients, and no validated screening test exists for average-risk adults. This topical review examines the biologic, clinical, economic, psychological, equity, and therapeutic evidence bearing on where scarce resources should be directed. The long interval between initiating mutation and invasive disease provides a mechanistic rationale for prevention and interception, and the modifiable exposures of obesity, tobacco, type 2 diabetes, and alcohol act largely within that window. We consider innovations that extend prevention beyond lifestyle advice-incretin-based weight management, risk stratification anchored in new-onset diabetes and biomarkers, and immunoprevention-together with early-onset disease, implementation and policy, and the barriers and evidentiary limits that temper these arguments. We propose a three-tier framework of primary prevention, early detection in high-risk groups, and therapy, and argue that research, policy, and clinical investment should be weighted upstream, because every case prevented spares the cost, capacity, and suffering that the downstream tiers must otherwise absorb.

records.abstractText:
Background

Curative-intent treatment for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma necessitates major surgery and chemotherapy, yet many patients do not undergo resection. Frailty may contribute to this phenomenon, but its prevalence and association with pancreatectomy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains poorly defined. This study describes the distribution of frailty and its association with curative-intent surgery in a nationally representative cohort of patients with nonmetastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

Methods

Using Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare data (2013-2019), we identified patients aged 66 years and older with nonmetastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Frailty was categorized as nonfrail, prefrail, mildly frail, or moderately to severely frail using the claims-based frailty index over the 12 months preceding diagnosis. We evaluated frailty distributions via kernel density estimation. We assessed the association between frailty category and receipt of surgery via logistic regression.

Results

Among 8237 patients (mean age = 78 years, 57.6% female, 77.4% White race), 2486 (30.2%) underwent curative-intent pancreatectomy. Surgery was performed in 39.7% of nonfrail and 30.7% of prefrail patients; after adjustment, prefrail patients had similar odds of resection compared to nonfrail patients (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 1.01, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.89 to 1.16). In contrast, 15.8% of mildly frail and 5.7% of moderately to severely frail patients underwent surgery; both groups had statistically significant lower odds of surgery vs nonfrail patients (mildly frail adjusted OR = 0.53, 95% CI = 0.43 to 0.66; moderately to severely frail adjusted OR = 0.18, 95% CI = 0.11 to 0.30).

Conclusions

Remarkably, less than 40% of nonfrail patients with nonmetastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma underwent surgery, suggesting that curative-intent treatment remains infrequent even among lower-risk adults. Frailty is also common and strongly associated with decreased odds of surgical resection.

records.abstractText: Ras-related C3 botulinum toxin substrate 3 (RAC3) is frequently up-regulated in multiple malignancies and has been implicated in tumor progression. However, its role in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains insufficiently defined. This retrospective case-control study included 69 PDAC cases treated with pancreaticoduodenectomy, 46 non-neoplastic pancreatic tissues, and 10 normal pancreatic controls. Immunohistochemical expression of RAC3, TGF-β, and Nestin was evaluated and correlated with clinicopathological parameters and survival outcomes. Results revealed that RAC3 expression was detected in all cases of PDAC. The nuclear RAC3 H-score demonstrated fair diagnostic performance in distinguishing PDAC from non-neoplastic pancreatic tissue (AUC = 0.77). Higher RAC3 H-scores were significantly associated with the absence of perineural invasion (p < 0.001), while increased cytoplasmic RAC3 expression correlated with lower tumor recurrence rates (p = 0.05). Positive expression of TGF-β and Nestin was significantly correlated with the absence of lymphovascular invasion (p = 0.05 and p = 0.002, respectively). Additionally, TGF-β showed a significant association with survival (p = 0.020; HR = 1.0231). In conclussion, RAC3 is frequently expressed in PDAC. Nuclear RAC3 expression may serve as a potential diagnostic marker. However, RAC3 cytoplasmic expression seems to be associated with more favorable clinicopathological features.

records.abstractText: The development of effective allele-specific and RAS-ON multiselective direct RAS inhibitors for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) represents unprecedented progress in systemic therapy for a devastating disease. These drugs are already changing the standard of care in PDAC, and their development raises important questions about how ongoing and future trials of local therapies such as radiotherapy (RT) may be affected. Although RT remains part of the therapeutic armamentarium for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), particularly in locally advanced disease and the adjuvant setting, decades of clinical trials have raised more questions than they have answered. One major challenge has been the concurrent evolution of systemic therapies, complicating the design, interpretation, and clinical relevance of RT trials. Here, we review how changes in systemic therapy have influenced seminal trials of RT for PDAC and will consider implications for ongoing and future trials in this space. These considerations, already relevant when options were more limited, are even more critical with the emergence of novel RAS-targeted therapies.

records.abstractText:
Introduction

Treatment sequencing is a major focus in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment in recent literature. A neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) first approach has been suggested to improve tumour stage and, in some cases, produce a total neoadjuvant response. However, in resectable disease, there are concerns that non-response or delay to definitive surgical excision could allow disease progression during this time.

Methods

This retrospective cohort analysis sampled cases (N = 152) of resectable and borderline resectable PDAC from a pancreatic cancer centre. Treatment demographics, chemotherapy and surgical outcomes, including tumour regression grade (TRG) and overall survival (OS), were compared.

Results

Demographic and disease characteristics differed significantly in ECOG score and radiological tumour venous involvement between NAC and UFS groups. FOLFIRINOX (57.3%) was the most common chemotherapy agent, and overall NAC completion was 53.3%. Disease progression during NAC occurred in 33.3% of cases, with 20% of those initially classified as resectable. In this cohort, the UFS group had a significantly improved overall survival compared to the NAC group (25.2 vs. 18.2 months, p = 0.03), which was not influenced by initial disease classification (HR = 1.03, 95% CI [0.10-10.41], p = 0.98). A significant correlation was found between TRG and OS (rs = -0.53, p = 0.005).

Discussion

Although TRG correlates with OS, this intention-to-treat analysis highlights the large proportion of cases, both resectable and borderline resectable, that do not complete NAC and do not receive surgical resection. This study did not identify any demographic or disease characteristics associated with favourable NAC tumour response.

records.abstractText: Patients with resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) can have different outcomes despite similar TNM stage. We developed TIGERS (Tumor Intelligence Grading and Evaluation Risk Score), a nine-feature prognostic biomarker derived from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. TIGERS quantifies tumor burden, glandular and nuclear morphology, chromatin texture, and tumor-stroma topology. The score was trained in 644 treatment-naive cases and evaluated in an internal validation cohort (n = 385), a separate post-neoadjuvant cohort (n = 275), two external cohorts (n = 260 and n = 235), the TCGA-PAAD cohort (n = 133), and a prospectively accrued external cohort (n = 155) with subsequent offline inference. Overall survival was the primary endpoint; the same formula and locked cutoff were applied throughout. The cutoff stratified survival in the internal validation cohort and three of four retrospective test cohorts. In the remaining external cohort, 226 of 235 patients (96.2%) were classified as high risk, showing limited transportability of the fixed threshold. Adding TIGERS to the clinicopathologic model increased Harrell's C-index in all six retrospective cohorts (range 0.015-0.047). In the prospectively accrued cohort, mortality was 47.5% in the high-risk group and 22.7% in the low-risk group; high risk remained associated with worse survival after adjustment (hazard ratio, 4.45; 95% confidence interval, 2.28-8.70; P < .001). Automated quality control passed 92.3% of screened cases, and scoring was completed in all included cases with a median turnaround time of 13.5 minutes. TIGERS assigned 43.2% of patients to a different risk category than the prespecified stage-based definition. Higher TIGERS correlated with a more basal-like proteomic profile in both the training and internal validation cohorts, supporting a molecular basis for its prognostic value. Routine H&E histology may therefore provide prognostic information complementary to conventional clinicopathologic assessment. Prospective interventional studies are needed before TIGERS can guide treatment or surveillance.

records.abstractText:
Purpose

Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest cancers in the United States, with most patients not being diagnosed until they present with symptomatic, advanced-stage disease. National trends in stage-specific PDAC incidence were analyzed to assess trends in stage-at-diagnosis over time and to evaluate whether advances in diagnosis and high-risk screening programs have helped shift detection towards earlier stages.

Methods

A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Patients diagnosed with PDAC between the years 2004 and 2023 were included. Age-adjusted incidence rates were calculated per 100,000 people. Trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression to estimate the average annual percent change (AAPC). Multivariable Negative Binomial regression was used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with stage-specific cases, adjusting for age, sex, race/ethnicity, and calendar year.

Results

Between the years 2004 and 2023, age-adjusted incidence rates of localized, regional, and distant-stage PDAC were 1.04, 1.26, and 4.94 per 100,000 population, respectively. Localized PDAC demonstrated the greatest increase over time, with an AAPC of 6.00% (95% CI: 4.96-7.49; p < 0.001), while distant-stage disease exhibited a small increase over time (AAPC 1.11%; 95% CI: 1.02-1.21; p < 0.001) and regional-stage disease did not change significantly (AAPC 0.27%; 95% CI: -1.18 to 1.92; p = 0.62). Localized-stage incidence accelerated further after approximately 2015, with APC increasing to 14.7% between 2015 and 2019. Similar localized-stage increases were observed across sex and racial/ethnic subgroups. In multivariable Negative Binomial regression, increasing age and Non-Hispanic Black race were associated with higher PDAC incidence, while female sex was associated with lower regional and distant incidence rates.

Conclusions

The findings suggest a stage shift toward increased diagnosis of localized PDAC over time. These trends may reflect improvements in imaging, surveillance of high-risk individuals, advances in endoscopic detection, and increasing diagnostic intensity, although rising underlying PDAC burden may also contribute. Further prospective studies are needed to determine whether these trends ultimately translate into meaningful improvements in survival outcomes.

records.abstractText: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable CT spatial phenotype associated with extrapancreatic perineural invasion (EPNI) in resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This multicenter study included training, internal testing, neoadjuvant testing, retrospective external testing, prospective external testing, and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) sets. The Preoperative Risk of Perineural High-risk Extension in Tumors (PROPHET) model and threshold were locked before testing. Performance was assessed with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and threshold metrics. Six radiologists compared unaided and assisted readings. A stratified Cox model related PROPHET risk to survival, adjusting for age, sex, tumor size, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, nodal category, and differentiation. Results Among 1854 patients (median age, 63 years; 1131 male), AUCs were 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86-0.96) in prospective external testing, 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.93) in retrospective external testing, 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.95) after neoadjuvant therapy, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.98-> 0.99) in internal testing, and 0.80 (95% CI, 0.68-0.93) in TCIA. TCIA sensitivity and specificity were 24/30 (80%) and 2/19 (11%). Assistance increased mean sensitivity to 93% from 82% and reduced reading time to 3.02 from 3.64 minutes per patient (both Holm-adjusted P < .001). Higher PROPHET risk was associated with shorter survival (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.53-2.47; nominal P < .001). Conclusion PROPHET provides a CT-visible tumor-vessel spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI. © The Author(s) 2026.
